scholarships.title: CLP Future Conservationist Awards 2027
scholarships.degree: Not applicable - professional project grant, no degree awarded
scholarships.official_source: Conservation Leadership Programme (BirdLife International, Fauna & Flora International and the Wildlife Conservation Society)

eligibility: Proposed projects must deliver effective conservation interventions for globally important, at-risk habitats and species through both ecological research and conservation action

Projects must fall within one of these themes: a) climate impact and adaptation, b) biodiversity conservation, c) habitat restoration and/or management, d) social development and wellbeing, e) Indigenous community participation and/or community-led conservation, f) environmental policy, g) human-wildlife conflict, or h) environmental education and citizen science

'At-risk' species are those categorised by the IUCN Red List as globally threatened (Critically Endangered, Endangered, Vulnerable) or Data Deficient, or where there is information indicating the need for urgent local conservation action
All team members must be early in their careers (i.e. have no more than five years of professional conservation experience)
Project teams must include at least three people and explain how each team member will develop their capacity through the project
All team members must be nationals of the country in which the project will take place, although one team member can be a non-national if this is clearly justified
Projects must take place in an eligible country (see guidelines)
Project duration must be between six and 12 months
Proposed projects must go beyond academic research and this must be demonstrated in the application
The total funding request from CLP must not exceed US$15,000
CLP funding must cover at least 50% of the project budget
existing.eligibility_summary: Early-career teams of at least three people, all nationals of the project country (one non-national member permitted if clearly justified), each with no more than five years of professional conservation experience, running a 6-12 month applied conservation project in an eligible country for no more than US$15,000.
benefits: Project grant of up to US$15,000 for the proposed conservation project
Ongoing support through CLP's global Alumni Network, including funding, training and mentorship
coverage: Project grant of up to US$15,000 for the proposed conservation project
Ongoing support through CLP's global Alumni Network, including funding, training and mentorship
requirements: Submit a Stage 1 concept note using the published CLP concept note application template
Follow the published guidelines on completing the concept note template, including the eligibility criteria
Meet all published eligibility criteria on the award page
Demonstrate that the project goes beyond academic research
Explain how each team member will develop their capacity through the project
Show that the total CLP request does not exceed US$15,000 and that CLP funding covers at least 50% of the project budget
documents: Stage 1 concept note, completed using the downloadable CLP concept note application template
application_method: Read the published guidelines on completing the concept note template, including the eligibility criteria
Check that the project country appears on the eligible-country list in the guidelines
Complete the downloadable concept note application template
Email the completed concept note to clp.applications@birdlife.org by 23:59 GMT on Friday, 30 October 2026
Wait for CLP to notify shortlisted applicants
If shortlisted, submit a full application through the CLP online application portal, following the Stage 2 guidelines
existing.selection_notes: Two-stage selection. Stage 1 concept notes are assessed against the published eligibility criteria and the eight eligible themes; only the highest-scoring (shortlisted) concept note applicants are notified and invited to submit a full application through the online portal. Late, incomplete or ineligible Stage 1 submissions will not be considered. Stage 2 detailed guidelines are provided only to applicants who reach that stage.
existing.best_fit: Early-career conservationists (no more than five years of professional conservation experience) who are nationals of the country where the project will run, working in a team of at least three people on applied conservation work on threatened species or habitats in one of CLP's eight themes.
existing.notes: CLP funding must cover at least 50% of the project budget, so the applicant must fund or raise at least the remainder of the budget from other sources. Total CLP request capped at US$15,000. Project duration must be between six and 12 months. Projects that are purely academic research are not eligible. No deferral, renewal, return-home or clinical-restriction rules are published on the award page.
existing.duration: Project duration must be between six and 12 months.
existing.application_period: Stage 1: concept notes due 30 October 2026, 23:59 GMT. Stage 2: only shortlisted (highest-scoring) concept note applicants are notified and invited to submit a full application via the CLP online application portal; detailed guidelines for the full application are provided to those who reach this stage.
existing.deadline_display: Stage 1 concept notes must be submitted by Friday, October 30, 2026 (23:59 GMT). Late, incomplete or ineligible submissions will not be considered.
